362586390.mission: Global Christian health organization that works to save lives and promote health.

programs.desc: Medicine and Health Supplies - In 2025, MAP International provided life-changing medicine and health supplies, positively impacting the lives of many. Working with 48 major partners, MAP provided medicine and health supplies in 100 countries. MAP International continued to grow and invest in the Bringing Children Health ("BCH") initiative and the Domestic Medicines Program ("DMP"). BCH nearly doubled the number of children with access to pediatric antibiotics, reaching more than 1,654,000 children across 40 countries. MAP's DMP also grew in 2025, providing over 346,000 treatments of prescription and over-the-counter medicine through 84 local free/charitable clinic partners across eight states (CA, TN, TX, GA, VA, IL, AL, FL, NC).

Community Health Development - In 2025, MAP's Community Health Development Programs reached more than one million people across Bolivia, Liberia, Indonesia, Burkina Faso, and Vietnam. In collaboration with local partners in these countries, MAP worked to improve health conditions through a robust mobile healthcare clinic (Indonesia), nutrition, immunization and vitamin provision for mothers and children (Bolivia), access to clean water and improved housing for health protection (Liberia), identifying and treating malnutrition (Burkina Faso), and raising awareness and testing for prostate cancer (Vietnam). MAP's Community Health Development efforts build on existing local capacity to improve healthcare access and quality of care for vulnerable populations.

Disaster Relief and Recovery - MAP responded to multiple emergency response efforts in 2025, including continued support in Ukraine, natural disaster relief in the United States and abroad, as well as responses in South Sudan and the Dominican Republic among others. Over 165,000 Disaster Health Kits for individuals and 8 Emergency Health Kits that support community needs were shipped to disasters and crises around the globe. A total of 10 countries were served with over $50 million in aid.

programs.desc: StreetLeader Program: Through our unique StreetLeader Program, UrbanPromise employs low-income high school students as counselors, tutors, and mentors for the children who attend our afterschool and summer programs. 521942990.mission: To assist Christians who are victims of persecution and discrimination and to come to their aid to secure their right of free practice of religion.

programs.desc: Assistance program: There is a spectrum of persecution from job discrimination to imprisonment, torture, and murder. ICC aids persecuted Christians that suffer along this spectrum to heal, withstand blows, and grow the church in depth and breadth in persecuted areas. Some of ICC's activities are as follows: - Aid to believers who have lost jobs due to persecution - Aid to believers whose communities are attacked - Aid to communities whose churches have been damaged or destroyed - Aid to those beaten for their faith - Aid to the families of martyrs ICC also builds the church by spreading the gospel and discipling believers in heavily persecuted areas: - Purchase and distribution of scripture - Financial support and training for church planters or underground pastors - Financial support of those pushing the gospel out via radio, internet, and various other means

Awareness program: As faithful stewards of God's word, ICC feels that it has been called to stand in a massive gap created by the church and the mainstream media and to educate those around us about the existence and severity of Christian persecution worldwide. ICC does this through press releases, newsletters, websites, social media, podcasts, various reports, and other means.

Advocacy program: ICC is working through government leaders in the U.S. Congress, the State Department, and the White House to support legislation, bring pressure on persecuting countries, and secure the release of the imprisoned. Advocacy is a challenging yet important function that ICC provides to suffering Christians, not because they believe they can ultimately stop persecution before Christ's return, but because they believe they have a scriptural mandate to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves.

Additionally, a growing number of active research clinical patient care, Gillette's research activities advance our mission to help children create their own stories.

204574040.mission: To ignite a passion for Jesus in students through experiences in worship, academics, missions, leadership and adventure.

programs.desc: Academic Program: Our first priority is to help young people, K4-12th grades, grow in the Christian faith. To accomplish this goal, we partner with our parents in the education process. Parents and students follow teacher provided lesson plans for Monday and Friday at home days. Tuesday through Thursday are at school days. Our elementary program for K4-5th focuses on the core academics. We offer a full course of study including Math, Science, Social Studies, PE, Language Arts, and Fine Arts. The secondary program consists of Junior High (6th-8th grade) and High School (9th-12th grade). In addition to the core academics, these students take Foreign Language, Computer Science, Adventure, and electives. We offer dual credit and online learning opportunities through online partner schools. USCO also offers honors.

Adventure Program: The Adventure Program is designed to teach students multiple outdoor disciplines and leadership skills that can be carried throughout life. Our vision is to cultivate lifelong servant leaders,united as a team to become more like Christ and strive to build skills that empower students to live adventurously in Gods creation. Along with classroom lectures, students spend ample time outdoors putting their skills to practice both locally and out of state. We teach canyoneering, mountaineering, rock climbing, ice climbing, backpacking, sailing and wilderness medicine.

Theater Program: The theater program trains students to use talents in acting and singing to build confidence and performance experience. Students are encouraged to use their God-given gifts to bless audiences. The skills they learn equip them to communicate effectively and confidently. They also learn all aspects of theater production: auditions, singing, dancing, acting, set design and creation, technical skills, strong work ethics, and public performance. This variety of experiences prepare students to advance into post-High School endeavors.

593445250.mission: THE ORGANIZATION IS ONE OF SEVEN REPRESENTATIVE SUPPORT OFFICES AROUND THE WORLD THAT SUPPORTS THE WATOTO MINISTRY (WATOTO). WATOTO IS A HOLISTIC CARE PROGRAM THAT WAS INITIATED AS A RESPONSE TO THE OVERWHELMING NUMBER OF ORPHANED CHILDREN AND VULNERABLE WOMEN IN UGANDA. WATOTO IS POSITIONED TO RESCUE INDIVIDUALS, RAISE EACH ONE AS A LEADER IN THEIR CHOSEN SPHERE OF LIFE SO THAT THEY IN TURN WILL REBUILD THEIR NATION.

programs.desc: SPONSOR A LIFE PROGRAM - THROUGH THE SPONSORSHIP OF BABIES, CHILDREN, AND VULNERABLE WOMEN, THE ORGANIZATION PROVIDES FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO WATOTO. WATOTO PROVIDES HOLISTIC CARE TO THOSE IN NEED IN UGANDA. THE HOLISTIC MODEL INVOLVES PHYSICAL CARE, MEDICAL INTERVENTION INCLUDING HIV/AIDS TREATMENT, EDUCATION - BOTH FORMAL AND TECHNICAL, TRAUMA COUNSELING, AND SPIRITUAL DISCIPLESHIP. SO FAR, OVER 1,000 CHILDREN RESCUED BY THE ORGANIZATION HAVE NOW REACHED ADULTHOOD AND HAVE GRADUATED THE PROGRAM WITH THE LIFE SKILLS AND EDUCATION THEY NEED TO BE INDEPENDENT. PROGRAM GRADUATES INCLUDE PROFESSIONALS SUCH AS TEACHERS, DOCTORS, LAWYERS, FARMERS, AND ENGINEERS, AMONG OTHERS. WATOTO IS CONTINUING TO RAISE TRANSFORMATIONAL LEADERS, WHO WILL POSITIVELY IMPACT EVERY SPHERE OF SOCIETY, REFORMING UGANDA AND SERVING AS A MODEL FOR THE REST OF AFRICA.

WATOTO CHILDREN'S CHOIR - THE WATOTO CHILDREN'S CHOIR HAS TRAVELED EXTENSIVELY SINCE 1994, SHARING A MESSAGE OF HOPE FOR AFRICA'S MOST VULNERABLE CHILDREN AND WOMEN. ON ALMOST EVERY DAY OF THE YEAR, THE CHOIR IS PERFORMING SOMEWHERE IN THE WORLD. THAT MEANS THOUSANDS OF PEOPLE GET TO MEET SOME OF UGANDA'S FUTURE LEADERS. THE CHOIR SERVES MANY PURPOSES. IT RAISES AWARENESS ABOUT THE WORK OF THE WATOTO GLOBALLY. IT ALSO PROVIDES LEADERSHIP TRAINING FOR THE CHILDREN, AND PROVIDES A STRONG SENSE OF RESPONSIBILITY WHILE EXPERIENCING DIFFERENT CULTURES. MOST IMPORTANTLY, IT'S A WAY THEY SHARE THEIR FAITH WITH PEOPLE AROUND THE WORLD ABOUT THE PLIGHT OF AFRICAN ORPHANS.

VISIT WATOTO - PEOPLE FROM ALL OVER THE WORLD VISIT WATOTO IN UGANDA. FROM CARING FOR BABIES TO WORKING WITH THE SUSTAINABILITY PROJECTS, THERE ARE A VARIETY OF MISSION TRIPS' GROUPS, AND INDIVIDUALS THAT CAN SERVE WATOTO. THE TWO MAIN TYPES OF TEAMS ARE CONSTRUCTION AND MEDICAL TEAMS. CONSTRUCTION TEAMS INCLUDE GROUPS OF PEOPLE OFTEN FROM CHURCHES, THAT TRAVEL TO AFRICA TO PROVIDE PRACTICAL HELP IN THE CHILDREN'S VILLAGES. THIS INCLUDES BUILDING HOMES, CLASSROOMS, OR OTHER VITAL STRUCTURES IN THE VILLAGES. MEDICAL TEAMS INCLUDE GROUPS OF MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS THAT GO TO AFRICA AND OFFER THEIR MEDICAL EXPERTISE TO TREAT THE BABIES, CHILDREN, AND WOMEN AND PROVIDE TRAINING TO THE MEDICAL PERSONNEL ON STAFF.

WATOTO UGANDA PROGRAMS- CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT, MEDICAL EQUIPMENT, CLOTHING, AND OTHER MUCH NEEDED SUPPLIES ARE SENT TO UGANDA VIA SHIPPING CONTAINERS TO PROVIDE DIRECT SUPPORT TO THE PROGRAMS ON THE GROUND. THESE PROGRAMS INCLUDE THE WATOTO VILLAGE, WATOTO NEIGHBORHOOD, WATOTO SUSTAINABILITY PROJECT AND FUTURE WATOTO COMMUNICATIONS- THROUGH PRINT COMMUNICATIONS, MEDIA PRODUCTION, AND SOCIAL MEDIA CONTENT, THE ORGANIZATION STRIVES TO SHARE THE STORIES OF THE ORPHANED AND THOSE AFFECTED BY THE HIV/AIDS CRISIS IN AFRICA. WITH KNOWLEDGE COMES POWER. PARTNER CHURCH- CHURCHES THAT PARTNER WITH WATOTO BECOME PART OF THE PROGRAM OF RESTORING WOMEN TO CARE FOR THEMSELVES AND THEIR FAMILIES, ORPHANS WELCOMED INTO THEIR FAMILIES, AND PLOTS OF LAND BECOMING SUSTAINABLE FARMING COMMUNITIES.

452256540.mission: The mission of For the Nations Refugee Outreach is to provide general education and family services that help meet the practical needs of refugees and to share with them the gospel of Jesus Christ.

programs.desc: Summer Reading Program: For the Nations summer reading program served 687 elementary children in small groups of less than 10 students per group for 8 weeks June- August 2025. The summer reading program includes English language learning, reading, math, Christian Bible teaching, and other extracurricular activities such as art, taekwondo, dance, music, coding, swim lessons, and needlepoint. Daily breakfast and lunch are also provided for children in need. Additionally, 21 refugee high school and college students were employed as interns over the summer to help run the program.

English Language and Literacy & GED Classes: FTN provides free, quality English & literacy classes as well as a GED class, which all include a Christian gospel message. These classes are offered twice daily (M-F) and serve 500 refugees from more than 20 countries from Africa, Asia, and the Middle East. Classes have excellent teachers and curriculum for English, literacy, and Bible teaching, which is noted by student progress. Student attendance is required for continued participation in the classes.

Preschool: For the Nations provides free, quality preschool for refugees children ages 3-5. Preschool is offered twice daily (M-F) and serves 120 students from more than 20 countries. Classes have excellent teachers and curriculum, which includes pre-math & pre-reading skills, art, fine and gross motor skills, and Christian Bible teaching.

After School Program: For the Nations also runs after school programs for elementary aged refugees Monday-Thursday, serving 160 youth. During the time after school, staff and volunteers provide help with homework,reading and math tutoring, snacks, supervised playtime, Christian Bible teaching and mentorship, and extracurricular activities such as art and taekwondo.

Child Protection and Family Strengthening: Conviventia works to prevent psychosocial risks and mitigate their effects on children. Our approach emphasizes equipping families with counseling, guidance, and practical tools to protect children from abuse, neglect, exploitation, or abandonment. We promote safer environments by fostering healthy family dynamics, supporting schools in their protective role, and mobilizing community leaders to be active agents of care. We advance this mission through family therapy, crisis intervention, and programs that restore broken relationships. By addressing root causes and promoting resilience, we help create protective networks where children can grow and thrive in safety and hope.

270950140.mission: The Institute for Family Studies is a nonpartisan research organization that produces original social science research and analysis on marriage, family formation, child well-being, and the cultural consequences of how the family is structured. IFS' mission is to strengthen marriage and family life and advance the welfare of children through research and public education. IFS publishes across three program areas, reaches our audience through a popular website, and provides widely respected information for journalists, policymakers, the academy, and the general public through reports, briefs, an
270950140.top_pay_title: Executive Director (Jan-March); Director of Family First Technology Initiative (Apr-Dec)

programs.desc: Get Married Initiative (GMI) GMI publishes original social science research and analysis on the state of marriage and how the family impacts individual and societal wellbeing. GMI produces research reports and briefs and provides expert commentary across a variety of live settings in media and legislatures.

Family First Technology Initiative (FFTI) FFTI produces original research and policy analysis on the impact of technology, social media, and artificial intelligence on family life in general and children in particular. FFTI drafts model legislation and is a leading public voice examining and evaluating tech regulation and debates across the country. Our research and analysis have shaped more than a dozen state laws concerning online child safety and FFTI fellows are featured regularly in media and appear in person as experts on these issues.

Public Engagement Initiative IFS reaches the general public with research and analysis through its website, earned media placements, and social media channels. During the fiscal year, our research and fellows were cited or featured in over 1,000 outlets including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, Forbes, the Financial Times, Fox News, NPR, and TIME. Website traffic doubled year over year. programs.desc: Residential and Non-Residential Services:A total of 481 guests were served in 2025 through our Residential Program at The Retreat in Wayzata, MN. The average length of stay for a guest in our residential program was 29 days. Sixty-five percent of the people participating were men and thirty-five percent were women with an average age of 47 years. The Retreat's Non-Residential Programs in both St. Paul and Wayzata served a total of 160 people in 2025, with 123 in our Evening Program and 37 in our 55Plus Program. Our Scholarship program assisted 579 people in 2025 providing $800,400 in scholarships. Teaching the essentials of recovery as embodied in the Twelve Steps of Alcoholics Anonymous and providing a strong focus on the basic principles of recovery are hallmarks of The Retreat philosophy. The Retreat creates an environment that promotes emotional and spiritual growth and helps establi

Sober Residences:The Organization operates six Sober Residences in the beautiful Crocus Hill area of St. Paul, MN. We offer 78 beds, 66 for men and 7 for women. In 2025 we served a total of 114 residents. The Sober Residences gives individuals the opportunity to put into practice the principles of recovery embodied in the Twelve Steps of Alcoholics Anonymous. With its close proximity to AA meetings, coffee houses and employment opportunities, residents become fully immersed in the recovery community and are provided the time structure and support essential to building a strong foundation of recovery. Housed separately, men and women work closely with sponsors to create a safe and supportive environment while establishing a solid foundation for recovery. Each resident commits to living at the Sober Residence for a minimum of six months. The fee ranges from $600-$950 per month.

Family Program:The Organization's Family program runs Thursday evening through Sunday at noon two times each month. In 2025 there were 220 people that attended the 4-day retreat either in person or virtually. Alcoholism is a disease that affects the entire family. THROUGH GENEROUS CONTRIBUTIONS, THE PROGRAM COVERED EDUCATIONAL EXPENSES, HEALTHCARE, AND ESSENTIAL RESOURCES, ENSURING THAT STUDENTS COULD FOCUS ON THEIR STUDIES AND PERSONAL GROWTH. MENTORSHIP AND GUIDANCE WERE INTEGRAL PARTS OF THE SPONSORSHIP, EMPOWERING EACH CHILD TO BUILD CONFIDENCE, RESILIENCE, AND A VISION FOR THEIR FUTURE. KEY IMPROVEMENTS INCLUDED INFRASTRUCTURE UPGRADES, EXPANDED CURRICULUM WITH LIFE SKILLS AND CULTURAL STUDIES, AND ONGOING TEACHER TRAINING TO SUPPORT DIVERSE LEARNING NEEDS. THE SCHOOL ALSO LAUNCHED A DAILY MEAL PROGRAM AND HEALTH INITIATIVES, REDUCING ABSENTEEISM AND BOOSTING STUDENT FOCUS. INCREASED COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT THROUGH WORKSHOPS AND FINANCIAL AID PROGRAMS ALLOWED MORE UNDERSERVED STUDENTS TO ATTEND, WHILE DIGITAL LITERACY EFFORTS EQUIPPED STUDENTS FOR THE DIGITAL AGE. FARM FRESH VEGETABLES ADDED TO THEIR DIET INCLUDING CABBAGE, PEPPERS, ONIONS AND BANANAS. programs.desc: Refugee Resettlement Programs:USA for UNHCR (U4U) raises funds and mobilizes resources to support Refugee Resettlement Programs. These programs are designed to provide a robust support network for refugees during their transition into new communities. They facilitate various aspects of the resettlement process, including initial placement, housing support, and comprehensive orientation about life in their new location.These programs also emphasize self-sufficiency by providing refugees with necessary tools and resources, such as language classes, job training, education support, and access to health services. U4U strives to empower refugees, helping them become active, contributing members of their communities.Furthermore, U4U works closely with local communities to foster positive relationships and mutual understanding between refugees and their new neighbors. The overarching goal is to

Gift-in-Kind Programs and Services:U4U's Gift-in-Kind Programs provide a platform for individuals, corporations, and other organizations to make non-monetary donations to support refugees. These gifts can include items such as clothes and household items, transportation services, and software licenses.U4U works diligently with donors to ensure their gifts align with the current needs of the refugee community. Upon receipt of donations, items are carefully sorted, organized, and distributed to refugees in need. This program not only delivers crucial support to refugees but also strengthens ties within the community, fostering a sense of unity and cooperation.

Refugee Awareness Activities:Refugee Awareness Activities aim to cultivate empathy, understanding, and support for refugees within the broader community. These activities encompass a range of public engagement initiatives, such as informative seminars, panel discussions, educational workshops, and cultural exchange events.By sharing refugee stories and experiences, U4U strives to dispel common misconceptions and promote a more accurate and nuanced understanding of the challenges refugees face. U4U encourages community members to participate in volunteering opportunities, advocacy campaigns, and other initiatives that directly support refugees.

200625750.mission: Servantworks challenges people to live radically like Jesus, by beginning ministries of service and sacrifice following His example, in order to transform families and communities. Our current focus is the hurting people of Thailand and SE Asia.

programs.desc: The WELL Program- Displays the love of Jesus to the broken, oppressed and poor of Thailand through material, relational and spiritual rehabilitation. Prostitution rescue in Thailand through the Well Program displays the love of Jesus to men, women and their families involved in the Thai sex industry through rescue and rehabilitation services that provide food, clothing, housing, addiction recovery and emotional healing through counseling, career education & training and spiritual development. Many of these services were delivered at the Coffee Shop community ministry that began in 2019 and has grown during 2024. The addition of Pastor Addy, through the Glass of Cold Water house church has greatly enhanced the outreach to younger adults.

Narimon Program/Community Center Bangkok- Provides women who have left the Thai sex industry a way to earn income while maintaining their dignity. This program provides alternative income-producing opportunities for women and girls who either once were forced to sell their dignity or are at high risk for doing so. The scale of this program was greatly reduced in 2024 to include a few women creating handmade products that they could be proud of. The products (mostly scarves) are sold primarily in the United States in conjunction with public awareness programs that encourage prayers and local law enforcement action against the Thai sex trade. The shift in product emphasis from jewelry towards scarves, convenience snack food products sold locally begun during 2018 has continued during 2024. The primary local sales venue is the Coffee Shop ministry site. Use of this easily accessed ground fl

Servantworks operates several smaller youth oriented projects including Grace Fund, The Well Children, Future Leaders, and Thailand Benevolence for youth. These various projects offer a broad spectrum of assistance to help at risk youth to turn from the typical journey towards the sex trade and to focus on education and careers that uplift the human spirit and allow for spiritual growth.

Previously a pilot program of The Well, the NAREE Sewing Project administered by Karati Sutter became an full time training enterprise during 2017 under the general oversight of our Field Director, Jim Larson. This expanding effort is currently managed and conducted by Servantworks associates under the name of NAREE within Thailand. At risk women and girls are offered training in sewing skills and provided a workshop with the tools necessary to hone seamstress skills in preparation for entering the mainstream workforce in Bangkok. This ministry continues to draw candidates away from the sex trade and into productive and respectable lifestyles. In 2023 a focus on men doing carpentry was added and tree farming was added during 2024.

Regional Meetings were held in Kansas City (September 2024), Boston (November 2024) and Los Angeles (January 2025). Speakers at the meetings include religious priests, religious sisters, bishops, diocesan priests and knowledgeable lay people. The IRL's internet visibility has grown with the year's numbers being 178,000 visitors on ReligiousLife.com, 166,000 visitors on CloisteredLife.com, 7,300 visitors on ReligiousBrotherhood.com, and 23,000 sessions on VocationBlog.com. programs.desc: In its 41st consecutive year, Operation School Bell provides new school clothing, shoes, and hygiene items to underserved Indianapolis students. Beyond the Bell provides a supply of new school clothing to schools; the students receiving these clothes are not otherwise served by Operation School Bell.

The Assault Survivor Kit program provides clothing for assault, rape, and domestic violence victims who are taken to hospitals and treatment centers and whose clothing is often retained as forensic evidence in the assault case. The kits consisting of a sweatshirt, sweatpants, underwear and socks, are delivered to 20 hospitals and agencies in Indianapolis and the surrounding counties. Hospital staff tell us that without this help, these victims would be released wearing hospital gowns and that these kits help to comfort the victims in their time of need and vulnerability.

Through the ALI Bears Program, soft cuddly bears are distributed to hospitals and trauma centers and also to shelters, hospices, and agencies serving adults and children in grief. Caregivers at these locations give these stuffed bears to their clients to ease their emotional and physical pain from which they are suffering. Having a bear to hug provides comfort during difficult times. ALI Friends offers companionship and caring to enhance the lives of older or disabled adults at two agencies. Member volunteers bring refreshments, celebrate birthdays, and play games while entertaining the residents and guests.

The remaining program included a pilot for a literacy program which included the reading of stories to 1st grade classrooms, discussions about the stories and distributions of books to the students and contributions to the school libraries.

programs.desc: Reception and Placement Program - The R&P Program is the 90-day initial resettlement period for newly arriving refugees. During this time, Exodus assists refugees begin new lives in the U.S. by assisting them with housing, food, and clothing; enrolling children for school and adults in English classes; taking clients to appointments with medical providers and social service agencies; as well as meeting other basic needs that arise. Exodus provides cash assistance to each refugee case to help with initial resettlement expenses. Exodus also provides staff to help identify community resources, develops training materials, and implement sustainable outreach programs for potential volunteer partners.

Refugee Support Services - RSS is a federally-funded program passed through the state that provides a variety of services to ORR-eligible populations. A main focus of RSS is employment, and through this program we complete service plans for employable clients, as well as provide job placement, job training, and case management services, among other services designed to help clients gain and maintain employment. RSS also partially funds English classes for clients. RSS contains a variety of set-asides that fund services to older refugees; youth mentoring; certain health services; and intakes and case management for eligible non-R&P clients such as secondary migrants, Cuban and Haitian Entrants, asylees, SIVs, and certain humanitarian parolees.

Matching Grant - Matching grant is a welfare-alternative program funded by the Office of Refugee Resettlement. It is designed to help clients achieve self-sufficiency within the 240-day program period. Matching Grant provides cash assistance to clients while providing a variety of self-sufficiency services, including service plans, job placement, and job upgrades. The agency is responsible for raising a certain amount of cash or in-kind match depending upon the number of clients participating in the program each year.

237267810.mission: To protect the natural diversity and beauty of northern Michigan by preserving significant land and scenic areas, and fostering appreciation and understanding of the environment.

programs.desc: The Conservancy's Stewardship Program cares for the nearly 30,000 acres owned as nature preserves and working forest reserves. Primary stewardship activities on these properties include monitoring, trail creation and maintenance, and ecological restoration work. In 2024, our Stewardship work included planting 7,627 trees, building nearly 9 miles of new trail, and improving 15 parking areas. Our ECAR (Ecological Conditions and Response) program inventoried over 17,000 acres and documented 1,334 species on our preserves.

The Conservancy's Land Protection Program works with landowners on a voluntary basis to acquire properties that further our mission of preserving scenic and significant lands. This is accomplished through acquisitions, conservation easements, and transfer and assist projects with local governments or the State of Michigan. Through this work, the Conservancy has protected over 70,254 acres since 1972. In 2024, we protected 1,186 acres. This included six projects in Emmet County, five projects in Charlevoix County, four projects in Cheboygan County, and five projects in the Upper Peninsula.

The Conservancy's Environmental Education Program offers free field trips, lessons, and activities to foster a greater understanding, appreciation, and enjoyment of the natural environment. Students can learn all year long through school field trips, weekend programs, and summer programs on Conservancy lands. In 2024, we led environmental education programs with 21 schools across our service area, impacting over 2,500 students. Additionally, we held bi-monthly programs with seniors.

programs.desc: The Foundation awarded university scholarships to 17 graduating seniors. All eligible seniors are invited to apply. To be eligible, the applicant must have attended Wylie High School their entire senior year and have maintained a "B" average. A committee consisting of 7 community and Board members evaluate the candidates based on financial need, GPA/ACT/SAT scores, references, school/community/work involvement, leadership skills and an essay. The scholarship checks are mailed directly to the registrar's office of the university for the benefit of the awarded student.

The Foundation awarded 22 Teacher Grants in 2024 totalling $23627. These grant awards will be disbursed in 2025. Balance of $59,883 funded in 2024 was for prior years' grants. All full time teachers in Wylie ISD are eligible and encouraged to apply. A committee of 7 community and Board members evaluate the candidates' request based on the potential to involve a great number of students and consistency with Wylie ISD's goal of increasing student achievement. The Major Objectives of the request are evaluated for definable and obtainable objectives and responsiveness to a stated need. The Activities/Implementation Plan is evaluated to assure that the project's methods are research based and are instructionally sound. Methods for Evaluation of the completed project are required.The teacher grant checks are mailed directly to Wylie ISD's accountant for the benefit of the awarded teachers. The

The Foundation welcomed 43 new teachers to Wylie ISD before school started and to recognize 7 retiring teachers.. Hendrick Health teams up with the Foundation to provide a luncheon for the new teachers and the administrators from each campus. The Foundation presents a $100 Mardel's gift card to each new teacher to help furnish their new classroom. The Foundation relates its purpose and the availability of Teacher Grants.

programs.desc: Urban Harvest's Food Access Program makes fresh, healthy food the easy, affordable choice for all through Double Up Houston, the Mobile Market, and the Saturday Farmers Market. Double Up Houston is Urban Harvest's SNAP incentive program in which food-insecure or low-income individuals can leverage enrollment in federal benefit programs, such as SNAP, WIC, and others, to access fresh fruit and vegetables at farm stands, farmers markets, and Mobile Market sites across Houston. Urban Harvest's Mobile Market partners with clinics, churches, schools, housing organizations, community centers, and other community-based sites to offer farm-fresh produce in low-income, low-access communities.

Urban Harvest's Permaculture Program builds advanced land stewardship skills and community leadership by training participants to design sustainable, regenerative systems that support food production, environmental health, and community resilience. Permaculture, or "permanent agriculture", is grounded in the ethics of Earth Care, People Care, and Fair Share. The program emphasizes practical application and long-term community benefit, making sure to include marginalized communities and community members.

Urban Harvest's Education Program builds the knowledge, skills, and confidence people need to grow food, care for the land, and participate meaningfully in the local food system. Rooted in experiential learning and community connection, the program integrates gardening classes, workshops like Edible Academy and Women in Agriculture, youth programming, and a robust Community Gardens network to support individual and collective well-being.

The Community Gardens Program offers access to shared growing spaces, technical assistance, leadership development, and a sense of belonging for nearly 4,000 gardeners. These gardens are critical to fighting hunger, creating a sense of community, and fostering ecological land stewardship. Urban Harvest supports the network of more than 175 community gardens through seasonal plant and material distributions, volunteer opportunities, access to classes and educational opportunities, and leadership development.

programs.desc: The Paul Carson Medical Program (PCMP) provides medical and economic development support. We focus on improving medical care by working with the medical directors and doctors who oversee the healthcare system of 5 hospitals, 120 clinics and a nursing school in the northwest region of Congo. We multiply impact by training Congolese medical professionals through our Medical Ambassador volunteer program. We aim to work with, not for, people who are making a difference in their own communities. PCMP is an active partner in training, financing and supporting this system and infrastructure designed to enhance the health status of some 3.3 million people in NW Congo. Village based programs installing clean water sources and community mobilization seeks to empower villagers toward greater health awareness and better health practices. Economic growth remains a crucial area of partnership because

Decades of neglect have made roads and bridges more barriers of transportation and in some cases impassable as only logs exist. Commercial transportation of goods has slowed, health care access has suffered, and people have been injured or died from some current bridge structures. PCMP and two other partners have focused on bridge repair/creation with the agreement of the Min. of Transportation. A basic design with predominantly local materials is utilized to replace dangerous bridges to allow any size commercial vehicle to pass safely. This is a program that utilizes the skills of national partners to create sustainable bridges for remote areas and repairs bridges on National Highway routes as well.

Economic development includes the Karawa Coffee Project. Launched in 2017, this project aims to work with 2,000 small-holder farmers, in more than 110 villages around Karawa in northwestern DR Congo. This long-term, generational effort enhances the productivity of existing coffee trees and intensify new coffee growth along with other food crops for local market and international export. Expected yield of 1,000 metric tons by 2026 . Reduces poverty, builds the economy, enhances food security. The Karawa Coffee Project has become a coffeee co-operative and is self-supporting.

Circles in Columbus is an initiative for persons living below the federal poverty guideline to work individually and as a group to develop personal and community plans to move out of poverty and become economically self-sufficient. Those who complete the 20-week program move into Circles in Columbus, a city-wide initiative to end poverty, which is housed at the Organization. These Circle Leaders (persons of poverty) are matched with 2-3 Allies (volunteers from the community) and together they work to implement the Circle Leaders plan to end poverty.

The Virginia D. Jackson Home for Women is a 10-bed facility for homeless women where residents may live for up to one year. Each resident must be employed, actively seeking employment, or attending school. The goal of the program is for each woman to obtain sustainable income and permanent housing. The Pastoral Institute provides individual and group counseling for the residents.

Welcome Home is a rapid rehousing program for homeless women and children and includes utility deposits, up to six-months of rental assistance, and intensive case management and six months of follow-up assistance.
